# ui-voice

WAV dictation or live voice through a provider, with ChatGPT Live, a local pipeline or a sidecar of your own.

- **Runs in:** the UI (your Emacs)
- **Source:** [lisp/ui/harness-ui-voice.el](../../lisp/ui/harness-ui-voice.el)
- **Loaded:** when enabled (see `harness-enable-modules`)
- **Requires:** [ui](ui.md), [ui-compose](ui-compose.md), [ui-media](ui-media.md)

## About

Optional, client-side speech, independent of the coding provider.
Providers declare a capability, `wav` or `live` (see
`harness-ui-voice-providers`); every command here dispatches on that
capability, and all providers share the chat, tools and permissions.

The WAV capability records a private WAV, transcribes it into the
current compose box, and speaks new assistant text sentence by
sentence.  Each utterance needs a click or key.  Mouse press/release
provides hold-to-talk; keyboards generally supply no release event to
Emacs, so their command toggles recording instead.

The live capability runs a JSON-lines sidecar that owns the
microphone, speaker and speech model, while Emacs keeps the captions,
the agent turn and every permission decision.  The bundled live
providers are ChatGPT Live (GPT-Live over the API), a local
whisper.cpp or Parakeet and Kokoro pipeline, and a scripted fixture;
a sidecar delegation becomes a distilled request in the chat (a
bounded piece of the voice conversation travels with it when the
request needs one), and assistant text streams back as commentary.
Audio never crosses the control pipe.

The local pipeline's speech-to-text model is a choice of its own
(`harness-voice-stt-model`), listed on the voice setup page: the
effort presets' whisper models, or NVIDIA Parakeet 0.6B through
sherpa-onnx.  Switching stops a live session and restarts the local
stack with the selected engine.

Commands are argv lists, never shell snippets.  WAV transcription prints
UTF-8 text; synthesis reads UTF-8 text on stdin and writes a WAV.  An
external player makes playback cancellable.  All processes run on this
UI client, even with a remote harness, and all temporary audio is removed
on completion, interruption, failure, buffer death and shutdown.

## Provides

### Commands

- `harness-voice` — Open voice controls here, or a quick voice chat from an ordinary buffer.
- `harness-voice-dictate` — Toggle dictation, or the live session, without sending anything.
- `harness-voice-hold` — Start dictation on mouse press EVENT, interrupting speech and the turn.
- `harness-voice-interrupt` — Stop speech, discard unfinished dictation, and cancel this voice turn.
- `harness-voice-release` — Stop the microphone and transcribe, on mouse release or keyboard toggle.
- `harness-voice-show` — Show the compose box that owns voice.
- `harness-voice-toggle` — Toggle voice in the current chat.

### Options

- `harness-voice-player-command` — Command playing a WAV, with `:file` for its path.
- `harness-voice-process-timeout` — Maximum seconds for one transcription, synthesis or playback command.
- `harness-voice-recording-limit` — Maximum seconds of one utterance before automatic transcription.
- `harness-voice-synthesize-command` — Command reading UTF-8 text on stdin and writing a WAV at `:file`.
- `harness-voice-transcribe-command` — Command transcribing a WAV into UTF-8 text on stdout.

## Uses

### Methods it calls

- `speech/synthesize` ([speech](speech.md))
- `speech/transcribe` ([speech](speech.md))

### Events it hears over ACP

- `harness/reloaded` → `harness-voice--on-event`
- `secrets/redacted` → `harness-voice--on-event`
- `session/redacted` → `harness-voice--on-event`

### Hooks it adds to

- `harness-compose-controls-functions` → `harness-voice--controls`
- `harness-ui-event-functions` → `harness-voice--on-event`
- `harness-ui-media-recording-blocked-p-functions` → `harness-voice--recording-p`
- `harness-ui-redraw-hook` → `harness-voice--redraw`
- `harness-ui-update-functions` → `harness-voice--on-update`
- `kill-buffer-hook` → `harness-voice--on-kill`
- `kill-emacs-hook` → `harness-voice--reset`
